A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Celo research and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Retained content can be matched reliably despite the changed title and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: Sections 5–6 and the appendices report original Celo meta-training, optimizer evaluations, component ablations and learned-schedule analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments and adds augmentation-level, scaling, runtime and AlgoPerf results. Original Celo/Celo-Adam outcomes are reported even though the AlgoPerf baseline curves use competition data.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, global task augmentation, the LSTM scheduler, the MLP update rule and two-stage meta-training remain unchanged. Celo-Adam in the new AlgoPerf evaluation corresponds to v1's existing Adam-update ablation in Table 3a. The additional augmentation variants do not replace the proposed default procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix A.6 adds evaluations on Fast MRI reconstruction, ImageNet classification, LibriSpeech speech recognition and WMT translation, substantially broadening represented datasets and tasks. These include Celo-Adam evaluations and reported full-Celo instability. The original four meta-training datasets and 17-task evaluation suite remain.

E2.justification: Schedule-Free AdamW becomes an evaluated comparator in the new AlgoPerf experiments, alongside the benchmark's tuned NAdamW baseline. Existing comparison sets remain unchanged. Table 5's change from 'pretrained-velo' to 'velo-4000' is a rename of the same comparator.

E3.justification: v2 adds meta-training horizons of 1K, 2K and 5K evaluated at 10K steps, a wall-clock-per-step benchmark, and AlgoPerf training/validation comparisons using task-specific metrics such as SSIM, accuracy, WER and BLEU. Appendix A.6 describes AlgoPerf's target-or-timeout convention. These are additional protocols; the original 2K-step evaluation remains unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's component and augmentation-presence ablations, Table 6 compares global, tensor and mixed augmentation across training stages. Appendix A.4 tests sensitivity to meta-training horizon and generalization to longer runs, while A.5 analyzes computational overhead. These substantially expand the questions investigated.

E5.justification: Appendix A.5 specifies 10 seeds per optimizer for the new runtime benchmark. Existing three-seed evaluation and meta-training disclosures remain unchanged; this is not an increase in their run counts. Table 7 reports point estimates without adding confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 retain their values, including Celo's final-loss IQM of 1.20 and speedup IQM of 1.86. New results include augmentation-level scores, 10K-evaluation IQMs of 1.85 for Celo and 0.34 for VeLO-S after 5K meta-training, runtime measurements, and AlgoPerf curves and instability findings. These substantially extend results under new conditions.

T1.justification: Appendix A.5 introduces a computational-cost derivation: 288 FLOPs per parameter for Celo's MLP and relative overhead of 48/B against a linear layer's forward/backward computation, excluding scheduler cost. The existing optimization equations and mathematical definitions are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, five introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same substantive claims about the three-part recipe, 24-GPU-hour meta-training, performance on unseen tasks, aggregate evaluation metrics and adaptive schedules. The added appendix evidence does not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: v1 offers general production-readiness caveats. v2 adds concrete applicability limits: full Celo is unstable on AlgoPerf workloads, while Celo-Adam generalizes but falls short of tuned-baseline validation performance. Appendix A.6 interprets this as a need for more robust learned update rules and scaled meta-training. A.5 additionally discusses runtime overhead relative to Adam.

D1.justification: v2 specifies the mixed-augmentation sampling choices and ranges, discloses the MLP's 30 inputs, two four-unit hidden layers and two outputs, identifies V100 hardware for runtime measurements, and states the provenance of AlgoPerf baseline data. Existing implementation instructions and code access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 7 adds targeted citations and discussion of stronger learned-optimizer baselines, hybrid nowcasting, and Thérien et al.'s µLO within Maximal Update Parametrization. It explicitly positions µLO as complementary. AlgoPerf competition and NumPy references are also added, without substantially changing the paper's overall research positioning.

P1.justification: The title becomes 'Celo: Training Versatile Learned Optimizers on a Compute Diet.' v2 makes localized grammar and terminology edits, updates author information and acknowledgements, renames Section 8, and inserts appendix subsections. The existing methodological narrative and main document organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds augmentation and runtime tables, an unnumbered scaling chart, and two six-panel AlgoPerf figures. Figure 5 gains a missing method legend. Existing appendix Figures 9–15 are retained as Figures 11–17, with surrounding layout reflow. The new displays substantially expand the visual evidence.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves evidence about practical applicability. v1's iteration-based speedups and smaller-task evaluations left runtime costs and larger-workload behavior largely untested. Appendices A.4–A.6 and Table 7 address these gaps, including negative evidence about Adam-relative overhead and full-Celo instability. The additional ablations strengthen support for design choices. Although broad headline claims remain and full-Celo AlgoPerf traces are omitted, the new measurements and explicit limitations materially improve empirical credibility and transparency.
